title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (p.17): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'contrée' (a 'region' or combinatorial tame space) by four pieces of data. (1) A set F_él of 'elementary figures', renamed 'multistrates' on the next page. (2) A refinement order X' ≪ X. (3) A symmetric 'compatibility' relation R. (4) A family of subsets called 'configurations' or 'figures', i.e. (locally) finite sets of pairwise compatible elementary figures. Construction 1 (p.17) defines X' ≤ X iff X' ≪ X and X', X are compatible. This is again an order, and two axioms are imposed. Fig_1: if X', X'' ≪ X are both compatible with X, they are compatible with each other. Fig_2: finite combinatorial dimension.

This page, Construction 2, defines dimension:
- For X ∈ F_él, consider the combinatorial dimensions, with respect to the order ≤, of all X' ∈ F_él that refine X (X' ≪ X).
- The combinatorial dimension of X' is read as the length of the longest strict ≤-chain ending at X'.
- The supremum of these numbers, assumed finite, is called the (figural?) dimension of X.
- The dimension of a figure, i.e. a configuration of compatible elementary figures, is by definition the sup of the dimensions of its constituent elementary figures.
- Equivalently, it is the sup of the lengths n of chains X_0 < X_1 < … < X_{n-1} ≪ X_n with X_n ∈ F. That is, a strict ≤-chain followed by one final refinement step into a constituent of F.

In modern terms this is a Krull-type (poset) dimension. In the model examples, elementary figures are (multi)strata of a tamely stratified space, ≤ is something like the face/closure order, and ≪ is refinement of stratifications. Dimension is then the maximal length of a chain of strata inside some refinement, exactly as the dimension of a stratified or semialgebraic set equals the longest chain in the face poset of a fine enough cell decomposition.

A marginal note dated 11 June reflects on the architecture. One could have developed the notion of (≤-)constructible parts, with union and intersection operations and a notion of 'domain' of a figure. Alternatively, one could treat the notions ≤ and compatibility separately as the primitives. So far he has put one relation in the foreground and derived the others from ≪ and compatibility. The next page goes on to 'lieux' (loci): the ≪-minimal multistrates, which are the points in the model examples. It then interprets domains in terms of sets of loci.
errors: Possible off-by-one or indexing ambiguity. In the chain X_0<…<X_{n-1} ≪ X_n, the final step is a refinement, not a ≤-step. So 'length' counts the ≤-chain inside a refinement, and the stated length n versus n-1 depends on convention. The note does not fix this.

Equality of 'sup over refinements of the ≤-dimension' with 'sup over such mixed chains' silently uses transitivity of ≪ and the fact that ≤ implies ≪. Both hold by Construction 1 but are not stated here.

Finiteness of the sup is assumed, which is axiom Fig_2. Nothing guarantees the dimension is invariant under further refinement without a monotonicity axiom: ≤-chains could lengthen under refinement. Such an axiom is not yet formulated.

ideas.what: Axiomatic combinatorial 'space' (contrée) given by elementary figures/multistrates with a refinement order ≪, a compatibility relation, and an induced order ≤
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial/poset model of tame (stratified) topology; cf. face posets, finite T0 (Alexandrov) spaces, o-minimal cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984), van den Dries, Shiota; poset models: Alexandrov, McCord
ideas.where_published: Only the programme of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this specific axiomatics appears unpublished

ideas.what: Dimension of an elementary figure as the sup over its refinements of the ≤-chain length; dimension of a figure as the sup over its constituents; equivalently the longest chain X_0<…<X_{n-1}≪X_n
ideas.modern_name: Krull/combinatorial dimension of a poset (stratification dimension via face-poset chains)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Krull dimension; dimension of cell complexes via chains of cells)

ideas.what: Plan to develop (≤-)constructible parts with union/intersection, and the choice of primitive relations (≤ and compatibility vs ≪)
ideas.modern_name: constructible sets / Boolean algebra of definable sets in tame geometry

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a purely combinatorial axiomatization of tame spaces. In it, dimension is defined intrinsically from two interacting relations (refinement ≪ and compatibility-restricted order ≤), via mixed chains <…<≪. Invariance of dimension under refinement, and the axioms needed for it, are left open ('axiomes convenables, à dégager').
missed.quote: C'est donc le sup pour les longueurs des chaînes (X_0, X_1, …, X_n) avec X_0 < X_1 < … < X_{n-1} ≪ X_n ∈ F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A combinatorial foundation for tame topology in which refinement of stratifications is part of the structure would be a counterpart to o-minimality phrased without a model-theoretic ambient. Abstract stratified spaces and exit-path posets fix one stratification; they do not make refinement a primitive. Modest interest; the thread appears not to have been taken up.

deep.surprise_reason: The general project (an axiomatic 'analysis situs' of contrées and multistrates) is little known and unpublished. But this page's content is a fairly routine definition of a poset/Krull-type dimension, plus a methodological note on which relations to take as primitive.
transcription_corrections: 'Féd' should read 'F_él' (F_el, the set of elementary figures).
'qui suffisent X' should read 'qui raffinent X' (X' ≪ X).
'dim. figure' is probably 'dim. figurale'; the superscript '(signe)' near 'dimension' is probably '(figurale)' or similar, not '(signe)'.
The diagonal struck line at the left is a deleted heading ('Dim. ...'), not 'Donc de ...'.
Top line: likely continues Fig_2 from p.17 ('... ou au moins le cas ...'); 'vraf' is a misreading.
The last lines suggest 'j'ai mis au premier plan [une relation], puis [...] la dérivation ≪, compatibilité', i.e. a remark on which relations are primitive and which derived.
